question: A new crew member opens the system map for a subdivision built in 2018. Which detail on the map tells the crew the diameter and material of a gravity sewer segment?
correctAnswer: The segment label showing pipe size and pipe material for that reach
explanation: Segment labels on a collection map carry the pipe size and material for each reach, which crews need before selecting cleaning or repair equipment.
options: The street name printed in bold type along the roadway centreline
The segment label showing pipe size and pipe material for that reach
The lot number assigned to the house at the nearest street corner
The colour used to shade the park block behind the row of houses
optionA: The street name printed in bold type along the roadway centreline
optionB: The segment label showing pipe size and pipe material for that reach
optionC: The lot number assigned to the house at the nearest street corner
optionD: The colour used to shade the park block behind the row of houses

question: A resident asks where the municipal sewer ends and the private service begins. Which feature most often marks that boundary near the property line?
correctAnswer: The cleanout or inspection chamber located at the property line
explanation: The cleanout or inspection chamber at the property line is the usual access and responsibility boundary between the municipal sewer and the private service.
options: The water meter installed inside the basement utility room wall
The point where the house drain changes from plastic to cast iron
The cleanout or inspection chamber located at the property line
The vent stack where it passes through the roof of the building
optionA: The water meter installed inside the basement utility room wall
optionB: The point where the house drain changes from plastic to cast iron
optionC: The cleanout or inspection chamber located at the property line

question: A manhole is overflowing onto a road during a heavy rain event. Which action does the first operator on site take before any repair work starts?
correctAnswer: Set up warning signs and barriers to protect traffic and pedestrians
explanation: Protecting the public comes first at an overflow. Signs and barriers secure the area before crews investigate or start repair work.
options: Set up warning signs and barriers to protect traffic and pedestrians
Remove the downstream manhole cover so the surcharged flow can drain
Direct residents to move their vehicles through the flooded lane way
Begin jetting the blocked segment from the overflowing manhole rim
optionA: Set up warning signs and barriers to protect traffic and pedestrians
optionB: Remove the downstream manhole cover so the surcharged flow can drain
optionC: Direct residents to move their vehicles through the flooded lane way
optionD: Begin jetting the blocked segment from the overflowing manhole rim

question: Before a jetting truck leaves the yard for a morning of sewer cleaning, which check confirms the unit can support the planned work?
correctAnswer: Read the tank level gauge and confirm enough water is on board for the job
explanation: Jetting work depends on the onboard water supply. Checking the tank level before leaving prevents a wasted trip and an unfinished cleaning run.
options: Check that the cab radio volume is set high enough for highway driving use
Confirm the paint on the hose reel matches the colour of the truck body
Count the traffic cones in the rack without checking the water supply level
Read the tank level gauge and confirm enough water is on board for the job

question: A lift station pump needs its coupling guard removed for inspection. Which lockout step protects the worker if someone else tries to start the pump?
correctAnswer: A personal lock is placed on the disconnect so it cannot be closed again
explanation: A personal lock on the disconnect physically prevents the equipment from being started again until the worker who placed the lock removes it.
options: A note is taped to the control panel asking staff not to start the pump
A personal lock is placed on the disconnect so it cannot be closed again
The start button is covered with a plastic cap that lifts off by hand use
A coworker is asked to watch the panel while the guard is off the coupling

question: At the end of a shift, an operator completes the log for a lift station visit. Which entry helps the next operator judge whether conditions are changing?
correctAnswer: The time of the visit, the wet well level, and any alarm or odour noted

A general note that the station looked normal with no readings written down
The time of the visit, the wet well level, and any alarm or odour noted

question: During a routine patrol, an operator finds a cracked manhole lid on a busy sidewalk. Which duty applies first?
correctAnswer: Report the hazard and make the area safe until a crew can replace the lid
explanation: A damaged lid on a sidewalk is a public hazard. The operator reports it and secures the area so no one steps into the opening before repair.

Leave the lid in place and mention it at the end of the month meeting
Push the broken pieces into the frame so the opening looks fully covered
Wait for a resident complaint before treating the damage as a real hazard

correctAnswer: Explain briefly what the crew is doing, how long it will last, and who to contact with concerns

question: A crew is sent to clean a sewer added in a recent subdivision extension, but the segment does not appear on the map they were given. Which update should be entered when they return?
correctAnswer: Add the new segment with its manholes, size, and flow direction to the map record
explanation: Maps stay useful only when field discoveries are recorded. Adding the segment, its manholes, size, and direction keeps future dispatch and planning accurate.
options: Write the new street name in the margin without adding the sewer segment itself
Wait until the next annual map printing and leave the field copy unchanged for now
Add the new segment with its manholes, size, and flow direction to the map record
Mark the nearest older segment as extended even though its size was never confirmed

question: Dry weather flows stay high in an older neighbourhood, and crews are checking private side sources. Which finding points to a private side inflow source?
correctAnswer: A sump pump discharge hose connected directly into the sanitary service line
explanation: A sump pump connected to the sanitary service sends clear groundwater into the sewer. That private connection adds flow even when no rain is falling.

A sump pump discharge hose connected directly into the sanitary service line
A downspout that discharges onto a splash pad draining toward the street
A basement window well fitted with a clear plastic cover over the opening

question: Sewage is backing up into a basement, and the downstream manhole is surcharged. Which decision best protects the home and the crew while help is arranged?
correctAnswer: Contain what can be contained, notify the supervisor, and avoid jetting into the surcharged line
explanation: Jetting into a surcharged main can worsen a backup. Containing the spill, notifying the supervisor, and waiting for the main to clear protects both parties.
options: Jet the service from the house toward the main at full pressure to clear it quickly
Open the basement cleanout and let the backed up sewage drain onto the floor area
Tell the homeowner to keep using water so the added flow pushes the blockage through
Contain what can be contained, notify the supervisor, and avoid jetting into the surcharged line

optionC: Tell the homeowner to keep using water so the added flow pushes the blockage through
optionD: Contain what can be contained, notify the supervisor, and avoid jetting into the surcharged line

question: Midway through a cleaning run, jetting pressure at the nozzle drops well below normal. Which check should the operator make first?
correctAnswer: Inspect the nozzle for blockage or wear and check the hose for kinks or leaks
explanation: A blocked or worn nozzle and a kinked or leaking hose are the most common causes of pressure loss, so they are checked before larger repairs.
options: Inspect the nozzle for blockage or wear and check the hose for kinks or leaks
Increase engine speed to maximum and continue the run without stopping the unit
Replace the entire hose length on site before checking any smaller component first
Switch to a larger nozzle opening and assume the pressure gauge is reading low
optionA: Inspect the nozzle for blockage or wear and check the hose for kinks or leaks
optionB: Increase engine speed to maximum and continue the run without stopping the unit
optionC: Replace the entire hose length on site before checking any smaller component first
optionD: Switch to a larger nozzle opening and assume the pressure gauge is reading low
sourceTitle: WPI: 2025 Need-to-Know criteria

explanation: With a personal lock for each worker, the equipment stays locked out until every worker has finished and removed their own lock.
options: The first worker to finish removes all of the locks so the pump can return to service
One lock is shared by the whole crew and the key is kept in the truck cab during work
Each worker places a personal lock on the group hasp and removes only their own lock
Workers sign a sheet in the office instead of placing locks on the disconnect itself

question: A high level alarm comes in for a lift station, and one pump is running when the operator arrives. The level is still rising slowly. Which action fits the operator duty in this situation?
correctAnswer: Verify the second pump and level controls, log the readings, and escalate if the level keeps rising
explanation: A rising level with a pump running signals a possible fault. Verifying the standby pump and controls, logging readings, and escalating protects the station.
options: Reset the alarm panel and leave, because one running pump means the station is under control
Turn off the running pump to check whether the alarm clears on its own without pumping
Wait at the station without recording readings until the next scheduled visit takes place
Verify the second pump and level controls, log the readings, and escalate if the level keeps rising

optionC: Wait at the station without recording readings until the next scheduled visit takes place

question: A homeowner asks a crew to enter the house and clear a blockage in the private service line. Which response respects the responsibility boundary?
correctAnswer: Explain that the private service is the owner responsibility and share how to contact a plumber or the office

options: Explain that the private service is the owner responsibility and share how to contact a plumber or the office
Agree to clear the private line with the municipal jetter so the resident does not complain further
Tell the homeowner the municipality will pay for any plumber they choose to hire for the work
Enter the home and attempt the repair, but leave no record because it is private property work

question: During a weekly generator check at a lift station, the operator finds the coolant level below the minimum mark. Which action keeps the station protected?
correctAnswer: Tag the finding, report it for service, and treat the generator as unreliable until it is repaired
explanation: Low coolant can cause an overheating shutdown during an outage. Reporting the fault and treating the unit as unreliable prompts repair before it is needed.
options: Tag the finding, report it for service, and treat the generator as unreliable until it is repaired
Top up the coolant with plain tap water and record the generator as fully ready for service
Ignore the low level because the generator only runs during a power outage at the station
Run the generator under full load for an hour to see whether the low coolant causes a shutdown
optionA: Tag the finding, report it for service, and treat the generator as unreliable until it is repaired
optionB: Top up the coolant with plain tap water and record the generator as fully ready for service
optionC: Ignore the low level because the generator only runs during a power outage at the station
optionD: Run the generator under full load for an hour to see whether the low coolant causes a shutdown

Start the pump briefly with the guards off to confirm it runs before locks are removed

question: Two log entries for the same station show very different pump run hours for one week. Which practice would have prevented this record problem?
correctAnswer: Record the meter readings at the time of each visit instead of writing them from memory later
explanation: Readings written at the time of the visit come straight from the meter. Reconstructed entries from memory are a common source of conflicting records.
options: Round every run hour reading to the nearest full day so small differences stop appearing
Copy the previous week readings forward when a visit is missed during a busy shift period
Let each operator keep a personal notebook and combine the numbers at the end of the year
Record the meter readings at the time of each visit instead of writing them from memory later

optionB: Copy the previous week readings forward when a visit is missed during a busy shift period
optionC: Let each operator keep a personal notebook and combine the numbers at the end of the year
optionD: Record the meter readings at the time of each visit instead of writing them from memory later

Close the street and excavate the main without checking any service connection points first

Advise all of the homeowners to pour hot water down their drains and call back next week

question: During a storm, two lift stations alarm at once, a road is flooding, and crews are limited. Which priority guides the emergency response?
correctAnswer: Protect life safety and public health first, then contain overflows, then protect property and restore service
explanation: Emergency response ranks life safety and public health above property. Containment and restoration follow in that order when resources are limited.
options: Protect life safety and public health first, then contain overflows, then protect property and restore service
Restore the station nearest the works yard first because it is the fastest one to reach today
Focus on saving basement contents at the first house that called before checking station alarms
Wait until the storm passes before responding, because conditions will be easier to assess later

optionB: Restore the station nearest the works yard first because it is the fastest one to reach today
optionC: Focus on saving basement contents at the first house that called before checking station alarms

question: A jetter pump begins to rattle and vibrate, and flow becomes uneven during a cleaning run. Which equipment check addresses a likely cause?
correctAnswer: Check the water supply strainer and tank feed for blockage that could starve the pump
explanation: A starved pump cavitates when its water supply is restricted. Checking the strainer and tank feed addresses a common and damaging cause.
options: Add more nozzle extensions to raise the pressure until the vibration smooths out again
Continue the run at full speed because rattling is normal for a pump of this size class

Drain the fuel tank and refill it, because fuel quality is the usual cause of this symptom

question: A pump has been locked out electrically, but the discharge line is still pressurized from the force main. Which hazard remains after the electrical lockout?
correctAnswer: Stored pressure energy in the line that must be released or isolated before parts are opened
explanation: Locking out electricity does not remove pressure stored in connected piping. That energy must be released or isolated before the system is opened.
options: Gravity flow in the wet well that stops as soon as the electrical disconnect is locked open
Static charge on the pump motor housing that grows while the equipment sits out of service
Heat from the control panel lighting that builds up behind the closed panel door over time
Stored pressure energy in the line that must be released or isolated before parts are opened
optionA: Gravity flow in the wet well that stops as soon as the electrical disconnect is locked open
optionB: Static charge on the pump motor housing that grows while the equipment sits out of service
optionC: Heat from the control panel lighting that builds up behind the closed panel door over time
optionD: Stored pressure energy in the line that must be released or isolated before parts are opened

question: After a sanitary sewer overflow, a supervisor reviews the event file for a report. Which record set best supports an accurate review?

Send a general notice asking residents to report themselves, with no field testing planned at all

question: A wet well holds 8,640 L above the pump stop level. The duty pump removes 68 L/s while inflow continues at 44 L/s. How many minutes will the pump take to draw the wet well down to the stop level? Round to 1 decimal place.
correctAnswer: 6.0 min
explanation: The net removal rate is the pump rate less the continuing inflow, so t = V / (Qpump - Qinflow) / 60. Substitute the stated values: (8640 / (68 - 44)) / 60 = 6.0 min. Round only the final result to 1 decimal place. The result uses the assumptions stated in the question.
